News – Capital FM https://capitalfm.africa News, Sustainability, Business, Lifestyle, Sports, Music and lots more Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:03:59 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://capitalfm.africa/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/cropped-cfmlogo-1-150x150.jpg News – Capital FM https://capitalfm.africa 32 32 Eastleigh building collapse death toll rises to eight as six more bodies recovered https://capitalfm.africa/eastleigh-building-collapse-death-toll-rises-as-six-more-bodies-recovered/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:33:31 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476597 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5- Rescue teams have recovered six more bodies from the rubble of a collapsed multi-storey building in Eastleigh, Nairobi, raising the number of confirmed fatalities to eight as the search for people still trapped beneath the debris continues.

Kamukunji MP Yusuf Hassan confirmed the latest recoveries on Thursday, describing the development as grim news for families who have been waiting anxiously for information about their missing relatives.

“Six more bodies were retrieved from the collapsed building in Eastleigh today. This is grim news, and my heart is heavy. No words can capture the grief of the families and communities struck by this terrible disaster,” Hassan said.

“We mourn with them, as we wait for the recovery of the remaining bodies inside the collapsed building.”

The latest recovery comes two days after rescue teams retrieved a second female body from the rubble, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to at least two at the time.

The National Police Service (NPS) had confirmed that four people had been rescued alive following the collapse, with a multi-agency team continuing search-and-rescue operations at the scene.

The first body, also that of a woman, was recovered on October 30, according to Hassan, who subsequently called on disaster management agencies to intensify efforts to reach those still trapped.

The latest recoveries point to a worsening death toll, although authorities are yet to issue an updated official casualty count or establish how many people remain missing.

Police have maintained that multi-agency teams are supporting the operation, urging members of the public to keep away from the affected area to allow emergency responders and specialised equipment to operate safely.

Hassan had earlier called for additional resources to accelerate the rescue operation, saying families were anxiously awaiting news of their loved ones.

The search operation remains focused on recovering those still believed to be beneath the debris.

]]> Court sets 2027 hearing for fresh challenge to Ruto’s Cabinet after declining urgent listing https://capitalfm.africa/court-to-hear-fresh-challenge-to-rutos-cabinet-next-year-after-declining-urgent-listing/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:21:48 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476596 NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 5 – The High Court has declined to certify as urgent a petition seeking to bar Cabinet Secretaries from exercising executive powers following the expiry of a court-ordered deadline for President William Ruto to reconstitute a gender-compliant Cabinet.

In directions issued on Thursday, Justice Patricia Nyaundi instead directed petitioner Eliud Matindi to serve the petition and an accompanying application on the respondents and interested parties by November 9.

The respondents have until November 24, or 14 days after service, to file their responses. Matindi has been granted seven days after service to file a further affidavit, but not later than December 2 ahead of a mention on February 10.

The petition follows a June 30, 2026 determination by a three-judge bench that found the composition of the national Cabinet fell short of the two-thirds gender requirement under Article 27(8) of the Constitution.

In a split decision, Justices Eric Ogola and Stephen Githinji formed the majority that directed the appointing authority to reconstitute the Cabinet within 120 days to comply with the constitutional gender threshold. Justice Jairus Ngaah delivered a dissenting opinion.

At the time, the Cabinet comprised 25 members, including the President, Deputy President, Attorney General and 22 Cabinet Secretaries. Seven were women, representing approximately 28 per cent, while 18 were men, or 72 per cent.

The majority found that the composition fell short of the constitutional threshold by two women, setting October 28 as the deadline for compliance.

Matindi argues that President Ruto failed to implement the directive within the stipulated period, despite there being no orders staying the judgment.

In the petition, he accuses the President and other respondents of disregarding the court’s decision while continuing to conduct government business under a Cabinet whose composition he considers unconstitutional.

“The President chose to do nothing,” the petitioner states, further describing the alleged non-compliance as a situation in which “the President of the Republic has challenged the Constitution to a duel and a battle of supremacy.”

To support his case, Matindi cites Gazette Notices issued on October 30 by several Cabinet Secretaries, including John Mbadi Ng’ongo, Hanna Wendot Cheptumo, Aden Duale, Julius Migos Ogamba, Mutahi Kagwe and Beatrice Askul Moe.

He argues that the notices demonstrate that the officials continue to exercise powers and discharge responsibilities reserved for members of the national executive.

“It is the petitioners’ case that, upon expiry of the court-granted compliance period… there is no national executive and Cabinet of the Republic of Kenya as decreed by Articles 130 and 152(1) of the Constitution,” the court papers state.

The petitioner is seeking conservatory orders to stop the affected Cabinet Secretaries from holding themselves out as members of the national executive or exercising the powers and functions of Cabinet pending determination of the case.

He also wants Executive Order No. 1 of 2025 suspended to the extent that it assigns statutory responsibilities to the Cabinet Secretaries in their capacity as members of the national executive.

The application further seeks to restrain the Controller of Budget from approving withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund or other public funds to facilitate payment of salaries, remuneration and benefits to the affected officials in that capacity.

Among the substantive reliefs sought are declarations that the President failed to comply with the June 30 judgment and that the continued exercise of executive authority by the affected officials is unconstitutional.

Matindi argues that allowing the officials to continue making decisions and exercising executive authority under a Cabinet he considers unconstitutional threatens the country’s constitutional order.

]]> Kalonzo’s Ukombozi tour attacked by goons in Migori https://capitalfm.africa/kalonzos-ukombozi-tour-attacked-by-goons-in-migori/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:41:50 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476585 NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 3 – Opposition leaders led by Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka were forced to condemn political violence after their Ukombozi tour came under attack by goons in Migori Town.

The incident happened on the final stop of the opposition campaign, which had earlier taken the leaders through Ntimaru in Kuria, Kehancha and Posta Grounds before arriving in Migori.

Kalonzo accused the police of using teargas against their supporters despite what he described as a peaceful political meeting.

“We need to do away with these goons. Why did the police lob teargas and yet we had a peaceful meeting? The script is throw the stones then teargas. It is very shameful,” Kalonzo said.

Kalonzo downplayed the number of attackers, saying they were fewer than ten, but warned that putting the life of a political leader at risk was a serious miscalculation.

“The great majority of Kenyans are saying one term. These were just a few goons, not more than ten, who started throwing stones,” Kalonzo said.

“But putting the life of a leader at risk is a serious miscalculation, and we condemn this. If they think they will scare us, then they are wrong.”

He said the attack had instead encouraged more Kenyans to reject political violence and intimidation.

“In fact, this now emboldens every Kenyan citizen to say no to violence and to goonism,” he added.

Kalonzo asserted that the country had turned against the government and was increasingly embracing the opposition’s one-term message.

“This is a sign that this administration has lost it and the whole country has gone one term,” he said.

The Wiper leader maintained that the opposition was now more determined to unite with other Kenyans and push for what he described as the liberation of the country.

“We are even now more re-energised to liberate Kenya alongside other Kenyans,” Kalonzo said.

Democratic Party leader Justin Muturi went further, accusing Suna East MP Junet Mohammed of being behind the attack.

Muturi described the incident as a deliberate attempt to intimidate opposition leaders and prevent them from engaging with residents.

“The attack on us in Migori Town by goons sent by Junet Mohammed is a blatant act of political intolerance and an assault on our democratic freedoms,” Muturi said.

He accused unnamed political actors of using violence instead of engaging in democratic competition, warning that the opposition would not be intimidated.

“This is the politics of cowardice and desperation. Those who believe they can unleash goons on opposition leaders and intimidate us into submission must understand that they have gravely underestimated our resolve,” he added.

Muturi said the opposition would continue speaking against injustice and offering Kenyans alternative leadership, insisting that their right to political engagement was protected by the Constitution.

“We will not be silenced. We will not be intimidated. We will not surrender the democratic space that Kenyans fought so hard to secure,” he said.

The opposition team also included DAP-Kenya leader Eugene Wamalwa and other leaders.

Muturi called for those responsible for the attack to be held accountable, warning against normalising violence as a tool of political mobilisation.

“You may send goons to attack us, but you cannot intimidate the people of Kenya into surrendering their democratic freedom,” he said.

The leaders maintained that they would continue with their political activities despite the incident.

]]> Police officer missing after students attack KCSE examination monitoring team in Kisii https://capitalfm.africa/police-officer-missing-after-students-attack-kcse-examination-monitoring-team-in-kisii/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:37:16 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476587 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5- A police officer is missing after students at Nyabisase Mixed Secondary School in Kisii County allegedly attacked a multi-agency team investigating suspected examination malpractice on Thursday.

Corporal Leonard Siele was reportedly seriously assaulted during the 10.30am confrontation before his whereabouts became unknown, triggering a search as investigators moved to establish the circumstances surrounding his disappearance.

The team comprised officers from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) and the National Intelligence Service (NIS), who had visited the institution following reports of suspected examination irregularities.

Police said the operation followed a report by KNEC official Gioko Kanyi, who alerted authorities to suspected malpractice at the school.

Upon arriving at the institution, the team reportedly discovered a laptop hidden behind the school administration offices and alerted DCI officers from Nyamache to respond.

However, before the investigators arrived, students allegedly turned violent and attacked the police officers and KNEC officials.

During the chaos, the students reportedly seized a Toyota Succeed belonging to Corporal Siele, extensively damaging the vehicle and stealing personal belongings kept inside.

Siele was among the officers involved in the examination monitoring operation, alongside IP Peterson Amimo, PC Edward Onyango and NIS officer Boniface Muli.

DCI officers from Nyamache subsequently visited the school as investigations were launched into the alleged examination malpractice, assault on the multi-agency team, damage to property and the officer’s disappearance.

Efforts to establish Corporal Siele’s whereabouts are ongoing.

The incident comes amid efforts by examination authorities and security agencies to safeguard the integrity of national examinations and investigate suspected cases of cheating.

]]> UNESCO demands stronger school safeguards as bullying affects one in three learners https://capitalfm.africa/unesco-demands-stronger-school-safeguards-as-bullying-affects-one-in-three-learners/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:29:20 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476584 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5 -One in three learners worldwide experiences bullying every month, while one in 10 is subjected to cyberbullying, raising concerns over the safety and well-being of children in schools and online spaces.

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) is calling on governments, schools, parents and technology companies to strengthen measures to protect learners from violence, including physical harassment, intimidation and online abuse.

In a statement marking the International Day against Violence and Bullying at School, Including Cyberbullying, observed on November 5, UNESCO urged countries to invest in teacher training, effective reporting mechanisms and stronger digital safety measures.

The organisation warned that school-related violence in all its forms violates children’s and adolescents’ rights to education, while negatively affecting their health, psychological well-being and academic development.

This year’s commemoration is being held under the theme, Every learner safe and well: From promise to practice, focusing on translating global commitments into practical measures that create safer and more inclusive learning environments.

UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany said protecting learners requires coordinated action across education systems, families, communities and the technology industry.

“Governments, educators, families, communities and technology companies all have a responsibility to protect learners, both offline and online. This requires effective prevention and reporting mechanisms, sustained investment and accountability,” El-Enany said.

He reaffirmed UNESCO’s commitment to ensuring that children can pursue their education without fear, stressing that every learner deserves to study, grow and thrive in safety and dignity.

The agency is advocating a whole-school approach that integrates violence prevention with mental health support, teacher welfare, inclusion and digital safety.

It is also urging education authorities to strengthen mechanisms through which learners can report abuse and ensure that schools are equipped to respond effectively when incidents occur.

The 2026 observance also marks the beginning of the second five-year cycle of the international day, coinciding with renewed global efforts to end violence against children.

UNESCO will convene a policy dialogue for Member States at its headquarters in Paris to showcase initiatives supporting safe, inclusive and health-promoting learning environments.

The campaign comes ahead of the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children, scheduled for November 18–19 in Manila, Philippines, where governments and partners will review progress made since the 2024 Bogotá Ministerial Conference.

]]> Kenya Navy receives first equipment under Sh3bn EU defence support https://capitalfm.africa/kenya-navy-receives-first-equipment-under-sh3bn-eu-defence-support/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:09:26 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476580 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5- The European Union has committed Sh3 billion in military support to the Kenya Defence Forces (KDF), with the Kenya Navy among the main beneficiaries in a partnership aimed at strengthening maritime security and regional stability.

The first consignment of non-lethal military equipment was handed over to the Kenya Navy on Wednesday at its headquarters in Mtongwe, Mombasa, under the EU’s European Peace Facility (EPF).

In a statement, the EU said the Sh3 billion support was financed by its Member States and marked the first time Kenya was receiving assistance through the European Peace Facility.

“Today, Europe and Kenya take our partnership to the sea. For the first time, Kenya receives European Peace Facility support: KSh3 billion for the Kenyan Defence Forces, financed by EU Member States, with the Kenya Navy among the main beneficiaries,” the EU said.

The equipment is intended to strengthen the operational capacity of the Kenya Navy’s Special Operations Squadron, particularly its Diving Unit and Kenya Navy Marines, by improving personnel safety, operational readiness and effectiveness during specialised maritime missions.

The handover was led by Maciej Stadejek, Deputy Managing Director for Peace, Security and Defence Policy at the European External Action Service, alongside EU Ambassador to Kenya Andreas Peschke.

The development comes as Kenya and the EU mark 50 years of diplomatic relations and reflects growing defence cooperation between the two partners.

Kenya Navy Commander Major General Paul Otieno described the handover as a significant milestone, saying the assistance demonstrated the EU’s confidence in Kenya’s role as a regional security partner.

“Today’s handover under the European Peace Facility marks an important milestone in that partnership. It is more than the transfer of equipment. It is a tangible expression of confidence in Kenya as a reliable security partner,” Otieno said.

He identified piracy, maritime terrorism, illicit trafficking and illegal fishing among the threats requiring sustained cooperation between countries.

Otieno said no single country could effectively address the challenges alone, underscoring the need for stronger maritime surveillance, intelligence sharing and coordinated responses among regional and international partners.

He also pledged that the Kenya Navy would integrate the equipment into its training and operational activities while ensuring proper maintenance, accountability and responsible utilisation.

Stadejek reaffirmed the EU’s commitment to strengthening Kenya’s defence capabilities and supporting regional security operations.

“Today’s handover is not an isolated initiative, but part of our continued commitment to supporting Kenya as a key security partner in the region,” he said.

EU Ambassador Peschke said the assistance would contribute to protecting international trade, maritime resources and the blue economy.

“As we mark 50 years of partnership between Kenya and the EU, today’s handover demonstrates our shared commitment to strengthening maritime security and regional stability,” Peschke said.

Established in 2021 and financed through contributions from EU Member States, the European Peace Facility supports international peace and security through the provision of equipment, infrastructure and training to partner countries.

The latest assistance complements other EU security engagements in the region, including the European Union Naval Force’s Operation Atalanta in the Western Indian Ocean.

The partnership is expected to strengthen Kenya’s capacity to respond to maritime threats while contributing to the protection of strategic shipping routes and marine resources across the region.

]]> Kenya faces 85pc malaria funding gap despite drop in infections https://capitalfm.africa/kenya-faces-85pc-malaria-funding-gap-despite-drop-in-infections/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:40:50 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476576 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5- Kenya is facing an Sh15 billion funding shortfall in its malaria control programme, threatening efforts to sustain declining infection rates as international health financing comes under pressure.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale says the country requires Sh17.7 billion annually to implement its malaria strategy but has only Sh2.66 billion available this financial year, leaving an 85 per cent funding gap.

Duale raised the concern while representing President William Ruto at the High-Level Dialogue on Malaria Elimination in Gaborone, Botswana, where he urged African governments to increase domestic health financing and reduce reliance on external donors.

“Kenya needs KSh17.7 billion annually to implement its malaria strategy, against the KSh2.66 billion available this year, leaving an 85% funding gap,” Duale said.

He warned that declining international funding could reverse gains made in combating malaria, calling on African countries to mobilise domestic resources, strengthen partnerships and invest in local manufacturing of essential medicines, mosquito nets and other health commodities.

Kenya has recorded a 34 per cent decline in confirmed malaria cases, falling from 5.54 million in 2023 to 3.64 million in the year to September 2026.

Malaria incidence among children under five has also dropped from 194 to 119 cases per 1,000, reflecting progress in prevention and treatment interventions.

However, Duale said sustaining the gains would require predictable financing and stronger domestic capacity to deliver malaria prevention and treatment services.

Kenya is seeking to address the financing and supply challenges through its Universal Health Coverage reforms, with interventions integrated into primary healthcare, community health services and digital disease surveillance.

The government is also strengthening efforts to contain antimalarial drug resistance through the adoption of multiple first-line treatment therapies and enhanced pharmacovigilance.

Duale further called for greater African health sovereignty through investment in local manufacturing, noting that Kenya’s Health Products and Technologies Local Manufacturing Strategy targets domestic production of 50 per cent of essential health commodities.

He cited the country’s growing capacity to manufacture spatial repellents as an example of local innovation, with trials indicating a reduction in malaria infections of approximately 33 per cent.

The Health CS also called for stronger regional cooperation, including joint malaria surveillance with Uganda and enhanced coordination through the East African Community, arguing that cross-border transmission requires countries to coordinate their prevention and control efforts.

The Gaborone dialogue was held alongside the 36th Board Meeting of the RBM Partnership to End Malaria, chaired by Botswana President Duma Gideon Boko.

It brought together health ministers and global health financing partners, including Global Fund Executive Director Peter Sands and RBM Partnership Chief Executive Officer Dr Michael Adekunle Charles, to discuss strategies for accelerating malaria elimination across Africa.

Other participants included Botswana Health Minister Dr Stephen Modise, Namibia’s Dr Esperance Luvindao, Sudan’s Dr Haitham Mohamed, Equatorial Guinea’s Mitoha Ondo’o Ayekaba and Angola’s Carlos Alberto Pinto.

Kenya’s High Commissioner to Botswana, Ambassador Sabdiyo Dido, accompanied Duale at the meeting.

]]> Kalonzo names Matiang’i, Orengo to lead Ukombozi Alliance Council https://capitalfm.africa/kalonzo-names-matiangi-orengo-to-lead-ukombozi-alliance-council/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:30:44 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476569 NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 5 – Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka has named former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang’i and Siaya Governor James Orengo as Chairman and co-chair of the Ukombozi Alliance Council, downplaying divisions within the opposition as leaders reorganise ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Kalonzo announced the appointments on Wednesday upon arrival at Kisumu International Airport at the start of a tour of Migori and Homa Bay counties, describing the emerging political formation as a broader coalition bringing together leaders committed to challenging President William Ruto.

The announcement comes amid competing political initiatives within the opposition, with leaders exploring different formations and possible presidential arrangements ahead of the next elections.

Kalonzo sought to dismiss suggestions of a fractured opposition, insisting that the alliance was bringing together leaders with a common political objective.

“Those who are busy counting our disagreements should know that we are going to the people together, and the people are waiting for us,” he said, describing the movement as a “super alliance”.

He added: “This country has had enough of the predator regime. Komboa Kenya is what we are about, and with Matiang’i and Orengo at the table, we are ready for the work ahead.”

Kalonzo said the appointments reflected the experience and national standing of the two leaders, adding that they would help steer the alliance’s political direction.

The Wiper leader said both leaders brought valuable experience to the alliance.

“Matiang’i knows how government works and how to get it to deliver. Orengo has stood for the Constitution when it was dangerous to do so. Kenyans will see that in the Alliance,” he said.

Rebrand

The appointments mark another step in the restructuring of the Ukombozi Alliance, which emerged from the rebranding of the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition on September 21.

Kalonzo announced the change of name, saying the decision had been reached unanimously by the coalition’s leadership as it sought a fresh political identity and a more coordinated structure ahead of the 2027 elections.

The formation subsequently secured a key legal reprieve after the Political Parties Disputes Tribunal lifted orders suspending its registration process in proceedings involving Allan Jayuga Akivaga, the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties and the Wiper Democratic Movement-Kenya.

The decision cleared the way for the Registrar of Political Parties to proceed with the registration in accordance with the Political Parties Act.

The alliance has positioned itself as a vehicle for consolidating opposition parties and widening cooperation ahead of the next General Election, as different political leaders pursue consultations on a possible joint challenge to Ruto.

Kalonzo’s latest appointments signal an effort to bring experienced political and legal figures into the alliance’s leadership as it seeks to establish itself as a broader opposition platform.

]]> Governors demand revocation of 2026 Tourism Regulations over county licensing powers https://capitalfm.africa/governors-demand-revocation-of-2026-tourism-regulations-over-county-licensing-powers/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:30:01 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476570 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5- The Council of Governors (CoG) has called for the revocation of the Tourism (Tourism Enterprise) Regulations, 2026, arguing that provisions granting the Tourism Regulatory Authority (TRA) exclusive licensing powers undermine the constitutional mandate of county governments.

The governors say the regulations risk creating a conflict between national and county governments by transferring licensing responsibilities for tourism enterprises to a national regulatory agency, despite trade development and regulation, including business licensing, being devolved functions.

Appearing before the Senate Committee on Delegated Legislation, Narok Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu, who chairs the Council’s Tourism and Wildlife Committee, raised concerns over the scope of powers assigned to the Tourism Regulatory Authority.

Ntutu argued that the regulations must be aligned with the Constitution to prevent duplication of responsibilities and protect the functions assigned to county governments under the devolved system of governance.

“The Council recommended t comprehensive review of the Regulations, alongside the fast-tracking of the review of the Tourism Act, 2011, to address regulatory overlaps, clarify institutional mandates and safeguard the constitutional functions of county governments while strengthening intergovernmental coordination,” CoG said.

The governors also want stronger intergovernmental coordination to ensure tourism regulation is undertaken within the constitutional framework while maintaining effective oversight of the sector.

The dispute places the regulation of tourism enterprises at the centre of renewed concerns over the division of responsibilities between the two levels of government, particularly where national regulatory frameworks intersect with county licensing powers.

The Council maintains that regulatory reforms should strengthen the tourism sector without undermining the constitutional responsibilities of county governments.

]]> WHO adds two experimental vaccines to Ebola trial targeting deadly Bundibugyo strain https://capitalfm.africa/who-adds-two-experimental-vaccines-to-ebola-trial-targeting-deadly-bundibugyo-strain/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=feed-news Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:18:02 +0000 https://capitalfm.africa/?p=1476568 NAIROBI,Kenya, Nov 5- The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended the addition of two experimental vaccines specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola to an ongoing clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), expanding efforts to develop protection against the virus driving the current outbreak.

The vaccines, ChAdOx1, developed by the University of Oxford in partnership with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469, are set to join the Tumaini clinical trial following national regulatory approvals.

The recommendation, made this week by WHO’s independent Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccines Prioritization, marks the first time vaccines specifically developed against the Bundibugyo virus will be evaluated during an outbreak of the disease.

The move comes as researchers intensify efforts to establish the safety and effectiveness of vaccines against a strain for which existing Ebola vaccines have not been established to provide protection.

WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the progress demonstrated the importance of scientific collaboration and investments in vaccine development.

“The fact that these vaccines are ready to enter clinical trials is a testament to the power of science and partnership,” Tedros said.

He, however, cautioned that vaccination alone would not be sufficient to end the outbreak, describing vaccines as a potential additional tool in controlling the disease.

The Tumaini trial, led by the DRC’s Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB), uses a ring-vaccination approach that targets contacts of people confirmed to have Bundibugyo virus disease.

The approach builds on lessons from the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak, when a landmark clinical trial in Guinea established the efficacy of Ervebo against the Zaire ebolavirus strain.

Ervebo is already being evaluated in the Tumaini trial to establish its effectiveness against Bundibugyo virus, with four vaccination rings established and several others being prepared.

The rings include contacts of people who have fallen ill or died from the infection.

Beyond vaccine development, WHO is also supporting trials investigating potential treatments for patients infected with the virus.

The PARTNERS trial, launched in July, is assessing whether the monoclonal antibody MBP134, the antiviral drug remdesivir or a combination of both can improve survival among patients with confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease.

Researchers also plan to introduce maftivimab into the trial, while a separate post-exposure prophylaxis study is evaluating obeldevisir as a potential intervention for people exposed to the virus.

WHO said initial findings from the treatment studies are expected in the coming months, while results from the vaccine trial are anticipated in early 2027.

The research is being supported through WHO’s Research and Development Blueprint and Health Emergencies Programme, which are coordinating scientific partnerships, technical guidance and operational support to ensure studies are conducted alongside the outbreak response.

The vaccine development programme has received investments from the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), with the trial bringing together research institutions and health partners from the DRC, Belgium and other countries.

The expansion of the trials is expected to generate evidence on potential vaccines and treatments against Bundibugyo virus, an Ebola strain that requires targeted research to establish effective medical countermeasures.
